However, better to consider: after trade I'd have 0 A, 1 B, 0 C - same variety count as before (1 good type owned). Since goods I have less of are more valuable, currently A count=1, B count=0 - B is more valuable to acquire. Trading A(which I have) for B(which I lack) increases marginal utility since B was scarce (0) becoming owned, while A goes from 1 to 0. Net variety stays at 1 type owned, but this opens diversification path for future trades. Accepting is neutral-to-positive as it aligns with obtaining scarce goods first.
